correctness.rationale: Definition 1.1 and the staircase coding fix the tilt-to-pressure normalization \(\eta=t/2\). Theorem 1.25 and Proposition 11.7 yield pressure parameters converging to \(\eta\). Proposition 8.9 gives \(P_n'(0)=O(1)\), while Proposition 8.10 plus Lemma 11.5 give \(P_n''(u)\asymp n\) uniformly on a bounded interval. A mean-value argument therefore forces the renormalized height to have the sign of \(t\) and linear magnitude. Theorem 4.5 gives the exact half-sign-sum identity; bounded increments extend the estimate from block indices to all indices. Theorems 1.9 and 1.10 then give \(A_n=\operatorname{sgn}(t)\,\Theta(\log n)\) and \(B_n\asymp\sqrt{\log n}\).

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp strength hierarchy among bias mechanisms. Generic global bias can occur at sublinear sign-drift scales, whereas nonzero exponential local tilt forces linear sign drift, fixes its eventual sign, and pushes the temporal central-limit center to the maximal allowed logarithmic order. This converts a local fixed-level frequency asymmetry into a global quantitative displacement law for the full bounded-type exponential-tilt class.
